mustMemorizeFacts: **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep | **Revision Effort:** ~10 min | **Category:** RBI & Monetary Policy
**Source:** CGB Mentors & Smartkeeda | **Event Date:** August 3–5, 2026
*What Happened**
The 6-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), chaired by **Governor Sanjay Malhotra**, kept the Policy Repo Rate unchanged at **5.25%**.
External Members: Dr. Nagesh Kumar, Saugata Bhattacharya, Prof. Ram Singh.
Internal Members: Sanjay Malhotra (Governor), Dr. Poonam Gupta, Indranil Bhattacharyya.
*Must Memorize (Core Exam Numbers)**
Policy Repo Rate: `5.25%` (Unchanged).
Core Inflation (FY27): Projected at **4.3%**.
External Stability: Q1 Gross FDI at **$30.7 billion**; Forex reserves cover **$>10$ months** of imports; External debt cover at **90.8%**.
*Know / Understand**
Core inflation is anchored at 4.3%, but food supply risks (El Niño disruptions affecting pulses and vegetables) prevent premature monetary easing.
⚠️ **Change-Sensitive:** Next MPC meeting scheduled for October 5–7, 2026.

62nd-rbi-monetary-policy-committee-mpc-m.contentMarkdown:
### 1. 62nd RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) Meeting (August 2026)
* **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep | **Revision Effort:** ~10 min | **Category:** RBI & Monetary Policy
* **Source:** CGB Mentors & Smartkeeda | **Event Date:** August 3–5, 2026

**What Happened**
* The 6-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), chaired by **Governor Sanjay Malhotra**, kept the Policy Repo Rate unchanged at **5.25%**.
* **External Members**: Dr. Nagesh Kumar, Saugata Bhattacharya, Prof. Ram Singh.
* **Internal Members**: Sanjay Malhotra (Governor), Dr. Poonam Gupta, Indranil Bhattacharyya.

**Must Memorize (Core Exam Numbers)**
* **Policy Repo Rate**: `5.25%` (Unchanged).
* **Real GDP Growth (FY 2026–27)**: Projected at **6.7%** ($Q_1$: 7.0%, $Q_2$: 6.4%, $Q_3$: 6.5%, $Q_4$: 6.8%).
* **CPI Inflation (FY 2026–27)**: Lowered to **5.0%** (earlier 5.1%) ($Q_2$: 4.7%, $Q_3$: 5.9%, $Q_4$: 5.5%).
* **Core Inflation (FY27)**: Projected at **4.3%**.
* **External Stability**: Q1 Gross FDI at **$30.7 billion**; Forex reserves cover **$>10$ months** of imports; External debt cover at **90.8%**.

**Know / Understand**
* Core inflation is anchored at 4.3%, but food supply risks (El Niño disruptions affecting pulses and vegetables) prevent premature monetary easing.
* ⚠️ **Change-Sensitive:** Next MPC meeting scheduled for October 5–7, 2026.

Operating Track Record: Minimum **10 years** of continuous operations.
Deposit Base: Minimum **₹10,000 crore** (audited as of March 31 of previous FY).
Net Worth: Minimum **₹300 crore**.

rbi-defers-basel-iii-pillar-3-disclosure.title: RBI Defers Basel III Pillar 3 Disclosures to April 1, 2027 (ECL Alignment)
mustMemorizeFacts: **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Memorize | **Revision Effort:** ~7 min | **Category:** Banking Regulation & Basel III
**Source:** Smartkeeda (Aug 2026) | **Origin:** RBI Notification
*What Happened**
The RBI deferred the mandatory implementation of the revised **Basel III Pillar 3 Market Discipline Disclosures** from September 30, 2026 to **April 1, 2027**.
Issued **10 amendment directions** revising instructions for Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks (SFBs), and Payments Banks (PBs).
*Must Memorize**
Effective Implementation Date: **April 1, 2027** (First revised quarterly disclosure applicable for quarter ending **June 30, 2027**).
Core Alignment: Aligns market disclosure frameworks directly with the **Expected Credit Loss (ECL)** provisioning framework and revised credit-risk capital rules.
Reporting Architecture: Applies at the **top consolidated level** of banking groups (non-top group entities provide standalone Pillar 3 disclosures).
Board Mandate: Banks must maintain a formal disclosure policy approved directly by their Board of Directors.

dfs-launches-india-s-1st-sovereign-backe.title: DFS Launches India's 1st Sovereign-Backed 'Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP)'
mustMemorizeFacts: **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep | **Revision Effort:** ~8 min | **Category:** Insurance & Trade Infrastructure
**Source:** Smartkeeda (Aug 2026) | **Issuer:** Department of Financial Services (MoF)
*What Happened & Key Facts**

DFS launched India’s 1st sovereign-backed **Protection & Indemnity (P&I)** insurance product under the **Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP)**, designed by **The New India Assurance Company Limited**.
First Policy Issued: Handed over to the **Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) Limited**.
Indemnity Capacity: Up to **$1.5 billion** available through the combined underwriting capacity of the pool with a 24×7 global port correspondent network.

Strategic Objective: Established to ensure uninterrupted maritime war-risk insurance capacity during geopolitical conflicts and eliminate reliance on foreign P&I clubs (reduced war-risk premium rates by **35–40%**; 1,608 policies issued by July 2026).

rbi-loan-recovery-directions-financed-sm.title: RBI Loan Recovery Directions & Financed Smartphone Lockout Norms
mustMemorizeFacts: **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Memorize | **Revision Effort:** ~6 min | **Category:** Consumer Protection & Digital Lending
**Effective Date:** **1 January 2027** | **Source:** CGB Mentors
*Must Memorize**
Calling Hours: Strictly between **8:00 AM and 7:00 PM** (No calls during bereavement/emergencies).
Mandatory Certification: All agents must hold **IIBF Certification**.
Smartphone Locks: No restriction before **30 DPD**; complete restrictions permitted only after **60 DPD**.
Protected SOS: Incoming calls, SMS, and emergency SOS **can NEVER be disabled**.
Restoration: Device must be unlocked within **1 hour** of payment; delay penalty = **₹250/hour** on the bank.

rbi-draft-master-directions-interest-rat.title: RBI Draft Master Directions: Interest Rates on Loans and Advances 2026
mustMemorizeFacts: **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep | **Revision Effort:** ~8 min | **Category:** Banking Regulation & Lending
**Status:** **DRAFT / CONSULTATION** | **Proposed Effective Date:** **1 April 2027**
**Verification Status:** Source-only (CGB Mentors p.6–7; primary-source verification pending)
*What Happened**
The RBI issued draft directions titled *RBI (Interest Rates on Loans and Advances) Directions, 2026* inviting stakeholder comments.
*Must Memorize (Draft Proposals)**

Benchmark Pricing: Lenders can offer loans at fixed or floating rates linked to an internal or external benchmark plus a risk-based spread. A lender **would not be allowed to price a loan below the applicable benchmark**.
Reset Frequency for Floating Loans:
The benchmark, reset frequency, and reset date must be clearly specified in the loan agreement.
The reset frequency is chosen by the lender, but **cannot be more than once every 3 months**.
Once fixed for a loan, the reset frequency **would remain unchanged through the loan tenor** (subject to specified exemptions for smaller cooperative banks, certain NBFCs, and some UCBs).
Agricultural Loans: Reset period linked to the crop season, but **cannot exceed 12 months**.

Internal Benchmark (MCLR): Commercial banks, RRBs, Tier 3 & Tier 4 urban cooperative banks, and rural cooperative banks with deposits $>₹1,000\text{ crore}$ would continue to use an internal benchmark based on the marginal cost of funds, referenced as **MCLR**.

External Benchmark (EBLR): Retains mandatory external benchmark linkage for all floating-rate personal loans and floating-rate loans to MSMEs extended by commercial banks (for RRBs, co-ops, NBFCs, and AIFIs, external benchmark linkage is not mandatory).
Interest Application: The draft proposes that interest on advances should generally be charged at **monthly rests**.
rbi-draft-master-directions-interest-rat.contentMarkdown:
### 1. RBI Draft Master Directions: Interest Rates on Loans and Advances 2026
* **Priority:** P1 — Critical / Deep | **Revision Effort:** ~8 min | **Category:** Banking Regulation & Lending
* **Status:** **DRAFT / CONSULTATION** | **Proposed Effective Date:** **1 April 2027**
* **Verification Status:** Source-only (CGB Mentors p.6–7; primary-source verification pending)

**What Happened**
* The RBI issued draft directions titled *RBI (Interest Rates on Loans and Advances) Directions, 2026* inviting stakeholder comments.

**Must Memorize (Draft Proposals)**
* **Benchmark Pricing**: Lenders can offer loans at fixed or floating rates linked to an internal or external benchmark plus a risk-based spread. A lender **would not be allowed to price a loan below the applicable benchmark**.
* **Reset Frequency for Floating Loans**:
  * The benchmark, reset frequency, and reset date must be clearly specified in the loan agreement.
  * The reset frequency is chosen by the lender, but **cannot be more than once every 3 months**.
  * Once fixed for a loan, the reset frequency **would remain unchanged through the loan tenor** (subject to specified exemptions for smaller cooperative banks, certain NBFCs, and some UCBs).
* **Agricultural Loans**: Reset period linked to the crop season, but **cannot exceed 12 months**.
* **Internal Benchmark (MCLR)**: Commercial banks, RRBs, Tier 3 & Tier 4 urban cooperative banks, and rural cooperative banks with deposits $>₹1,000\text{ crore}$ would continue to use an internal benchmark based on the marginal cost of funds, referenced as **MCLR**.
* **External Benchmark (EBLR)**: Retains mandatory external benchmark linkage for all floating-rate personal loans and floating-rate loans to MSMEs extended by commercial banks (for RRBs, co-ops, NBFCs, and AIFIs, external benchmark linkage is not mandatory).
* **Interest Application**: The draft proposes that interest on advances should generally be charged at **monthly rests**.
